scope: All 24 frozen evidence claims CORE-04 through CORE-06. Historical support is separate from temporal availability and epistemic status. No claim is certified by a bibliography alone.

status_semantics.supported: Read source supports historical proposition; independent temporal and source-type caveats still apply.
status_semantics.partially_supported: At least one clause or quantifier goes beyond read support.
status_semantics.inference: Reasonable interpretation/counterfactual rather than verified observed fact; supporting material does not establish entire inference.
status_semantics.unverified_access: No usable direct support obtained because access failed.
status_semantics.unsupported: Read sources fail to support or contradict the claim.

limitations: Original NSW 1915 Act inaccessible; reconstructed statutory extracts were read. January bill version and debate dates unverified.

No contemporaneous Swedish admission decision, border order or cabinet capacity assessment inspected. Exact 2 October announcement date remains manifest-specified rather than independently verified here.
Search returned irrelevant results on several attempts; those results were not used.
Modern sources and post-event factual reconstructions are not represented as documents available to original decision-makers.
No outcome totals or later harms imported to support predecision claims.
No runtime, frozen pack, constitution or historical ledger changed. No live evaluator calls.

claims.claim: Under existing law, involuntary removal of a child in the protected population on neglect grounds requires the Board to establish neglect through a court process.

sources.locator: Segregation and merging, paragraph on 1909 Act (web lines 59-60)

claims.paraphrased_support: The inquiry describes a court-neglect route before removal and separate apprenticeship powers.
claims.decision_time_assessment: Claims are historically reconstructed; the January 1915 cutoff has no exact day or inspected bill/Hansard version. The enacted Act is dated 15 February. Do not silently treat final statutory wording or undated 1915 debate as already available in January.
claims.epistemic_assessment: Historical legal statement; observed in documentary reconstruction, not direct observation.
claims.recommendation: Retain with a citation and qualify as removal on neglect grounds, avoiding a universal claim covering every custody route.

claims.claim: The Board and government say the court requirement makes separation difficult and slow, including where officials regard a child's surroundings as morally undesirable but the child is clothed, fed or otherwise not readily provable as neglected; families can also move before proceedings finish.

sources.locator: Full control and custody, paragraphs citing Colonial Secretary and Parliamentary Debates 1914-15 (lines 66-69)

claims.paraphrased_support: Attributed official complaints concern evidential difficulty, delay, parental resistance and movement across the border.
claims.decision_time_assessment: Claims are historically reconstructed; the January 1915 cutoff has no exact day or inspected bill/Hansard version. The enacted Act is dated 15 February. Do not silently treat final statutory wording or undated 1915 debate as already available in January.
claims.epistemic_assessment: Interested institutional assertions, accurately marked reported.
claims.recommendation: Keep reported; cite each attributed rationale. Do not turn officials' objections into proof of actual child danger.

claims.decision_time_assessment: Claims are historically reconstructed; the January 1915 cutoff has no exact day or inspected bill/Hansard version. The enacted Act is dated 15 February. Do not silently treat final statutory wording or undated 1915 debate as already available in January.
claims.epistemic_assessment: Documentary proposition supported through official statutory reconstruction; original Act access failed.
claims.recommendation: Attach the provision; obtain the January bill before claiming exact cutoff verification. Preserve legally defined population rather than reducing classification to biology alone.

claims.claim: The country's preceding constitutional tradition stated equality before law and rejected public-law privilege or disadvantage based on birth or rank.

sources.locator: Article 109 (lines 182-190)

claims.paraphrased_support: Article 109 sets equality and rejects inherited public-law privilege.
claims.decision_time_assessment: The relevant text existed at the 15 September 1935 legislative decision. Use original-law provisions only; exclude November ancestry decree and subsequent persecution outcomes.
claims.epistemic_assessment: Primary constitutional text supports the limited historical claim.
claims.recommendation: Retain preceding tradition wording; do not imply those protections were effective in 1935.

claims.claim: No individualised evidential test is supplied connecting minority status, ancestry or a consensual intimate relationship to a concrete harmful act ordinarily relevant to loss of citizenship or civil rights.

claims.decision_time_assessment: The relevant text existed at the 15 September 1935 legislative decision. Use original-law provisions only; exclude November ancestry decree and subsequent persecution outcomes.
claims.epistemic_assessment: Negative textual finding plus normative comparator, overstated as observed.
claims.recommendation: Relabel textual inference. Separate the verifiable absence of such a test from the normative phrase ordinarily relevant.

claims.claim: Occupation/security authorities are preparing and beginning a coordinated operation to arrest members of the targeted minority and deport them from the occupied country.

sources.locator: Denmark section, warning and scheduled operation (line 142)

claims.paraphrased_support: The museum dates a warning to 28 September and the planned deportation operation to 1-2 October.
claims.decision_time_assessment: The 28 September warning and scheduled 1-2 October operation precede or overlap the 2 October cutoff. No contemporaneous Swedish cabinet, border order, or asylum announcement was inspected; later historical reconstruction does not establish precisely what ministers knew at a specified hour.
claims.epistemic_assessment: Later reconstruction of a contemporaneous warning, not direct intelligence record.
claims.recommendation: Retain reported; specify whether cutoff is before or after the operation began. Exclude later deportee outcomes.

claims.claim: Many members of the minority are going into hiding and need a destination outside the occupier's control if they are to evade arrest.

sources.locator: Denmark section, hiding and evacuation (line 143)

claims.decision_time_assessment: The 28 September warning and scheduled 1-2 October operation precede or overlap the 2 October cutoff. claims.epistemic_assessment: Compound claim combines historical observation with a strategic necessity inference.
claims.recommendation: Split observed hiding from inference that external refuge was necessary for durable safety. Avoid implying nobody could evade arrest within Denmark.

claims.claim: Refusing admission or leaving entry materially uncertain risks closing the most accessible neutral refuge available during the imminent roundup.

claims.recommendation: Keep inferred; replace most accessible with a nearby practicable refuge unless comparative route evidence is added.
